verifications.claim: The Dune saga was created by Frank Herbert.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Dune is an American science fiction media franchise that originated with the 1965 novel Dune by Frank Herbert"; "Frank Herbert wrote six “Dune” books"; "Dune Series by Frank Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly attribute the creation/origin of the Dune saga to Frank Herbert.

verifications.claim: The Dune saga consists of six original sci-fi novels.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Herbert wrote five sequels"; lists six novels: Dune (1965), Dune Messiah (1969), Children of Dune (1976), God Emperor of Dune (1981), Heretics of Dune (1984), Chapterhouse: Dune (1985); "Frank Herbert wrote six “Dune” books"; "Complete Dune Series Set (6 Books)"; "10 primary works" listing the six
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently state Frank Herbert wrote exactly six original Dune novels.

verifications.claim: The original novels are centered on the desert planet Arrakis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The harsh desert planet Arrakis, the only known source of the spice melange, is vital to the Imperium"; "the desert planet Arrakis"; "Set on the desert planet Arrakis"
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe the original novels as centered on Arrakis.

verifications.claim: The original series starts with Dune (1965).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Dune (1965) by Frank Herbert"; "The original “Dune” series includes... “Dune” by Frank Herbert"; "Book 1... Dune"
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Dune (1965) as the starting point of the original series.

verifications.claim: The original series follows Paul Atreides and his descendants through Dune Messiah, Children of Dune, God Emperor of Dune, Heretics of Dune, and Chapterhouse: Dune.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Timeline sections: "Dune (1965)... Dune Messiah (1969)... Children of Dune (1976)... God Emperor of Dune (1981)... Heretics of Dune (1984)... Chapterhouse: Dune (1985)" with plot summaries following Paul and descendants
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly lists and describes the sequence matching the claim exactly.

verifications.claim: Dune was published in 1965.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Dune (1965) by Frank Herbert"; "Dune (1965)"
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of publication year for Dune.

verifications.claim: Dune introduces Paul Atreides.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "As Frank Herbert's Dune (1965) begins, Duke Leto Atreides... the so-called 'Arrakis Affair' puts unexpected Kwisatz Haderach Paul Atreides in control"
verifications.reasoning: R1 confirms Paul Atreides is introduced in Dune.

verifications.claim: In Dune, Paul Atreides' family takes control of the desert planet Arrakis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Duke Leto Atreides finds himself... put him in control of the desert planet Arrakis... Paul Atreides in control of first the Fremen people and then Arrakis itself."
verifications.reasoning: R1 describes House Atreides (Paul's family) being assigned control of Arrakis, and Paul ultimately taking control.

verifications.claim: Dune Messiah was published in 1969.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Dune Messiah (1969) by Frank Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Direct publication date confirmation.

verifications.claim: Dune Messiah examines the consequences of Paul Atreides' ascension.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "With a bloody jihad subsequently unleashed across the universe in Paul's name but out of his control, the Bene Gesserit... conspire to dethrone him in Dune Messiah (1969)."
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly describes Dune Messiah as addressing consequences of Paul's rise.

verifications.claim: Children of Dune was published in 1976.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Children of Dune (1976) by Frank Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation.

verifications.claim: Children of Dune follows Paul Atreides' children, Leto II and Ghanima.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Though the plot fails, the Atreides Empire continues to devolve in Children of Dune (1976) as... Paul's twin heirs Leto II and Ghanima rise to power."
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly states it follows Paul's children Leto II and Ghanima.

verifications.claim: God Emperor of Dune was published in 1981.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "God Emperor of Dune (1981) by Frank Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation.

verifications.claim: God Emperor of Dune features a transformed, long-reigning Leto II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "At the time of God Emperor of Dune (1981), Paul's son, the God Emperor Leto II Atreides, has ruled the Empire for 3,500 years... transforming him into a human-sandworm hybrid."
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to description.

verifications.claim: Heretics of Dune was published in 1984.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Heretics of Dune (1984) by Frank Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation.

verifications.claim: Heretics of Dune is set centuries later.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "At the time of Heretics of Dune (1984) and Chapterhouse: Dune (1985)—1500 years after Leto's death"
verifications.reasoning: 1500 years is centuries later from prior books.

verifications.claim: Heretics of Dune focuses on the Bene Gesserit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the balance of power... rests among the Ixians, the Bene Gesserit, and the Tleilaxu. The Bene Gesserit, through manipulation..."
verifications.reasoning: Bene Gesserit are central to the plot in R1's summary.

verifications.claim: Dune was published in 1985.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Dune (1965) by Frank Herbert"; "Chapterhouse: Dune (1985) by Frank Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Dune (first novel) published 1965, not 1985; Chapterhouse: Dune is 1985 but titled differently.

verifications.claim: Dune concludes Frank Herbert's original series.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Chapterhouse: Dune (1985) by Frank Herbert" concludes; Dune is first novel
verifications.reasoning: Chapterhouse: Dune concludes the series; Dune is the starting novel.

verifications.claim: Brian Herbert is Frank Herbert's son.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "his son Brian Herbert"; "his son, Brian Herbert"
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated across sources.

verifications.claim: Following Frank Herbert's death, Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson wrote numerous prequels and sequels.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Beginning in 1999, his son Brian Herbert and science fiction author Kevin J. Anderson published several collections of prequel novels, as well as two sequels"
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm post-death prequels and sequels by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson.

verifications.claim: Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson wrote Hunters of Dune (2006).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Hunters of Dune (2006) by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match.

verifications.claim: Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson wrote Sandworms of Dune (2007).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Sandworms of Dune (2007) by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match.

verifications.claim: Hunters of Dune and Sandworms of Dune continue the original storyline.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "two sequels that complete the original Dune series (Hunters of Dune in 2006 and Sandworms of Dune in 2007), partially based on Frank Herbert's notes"
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as continuing and completing the original series.

verifications.claim: Legends of Dune Trilogy consists of The Butlerian Jihad, The Machine Crusade, The Battle of Corrin.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Legends of Dune prequel trilogy (2002–2004) by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson: Dune: The Butlerian Jihad (2002), Dune: The Machine Crusade (2003), and Dune: The Battle of Corrin (2004)"
verifications.reasoning: Exact titles and trilogy name match.

verifications.claim: Great Schools of Dune Trilogy consists of Sisterhood of Dune, Mentats of Dune, Navigators of Dune.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Great Schools of Dune prequel trilogy (2012–2016) by Brian Herbert and Anderson: Sisterhood of Dune... Mentats of Dune... Navigators of Dune"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match.

verifications.claim: Prelude to Dune Trilogy consists of House Atreides, House Harkonnen, House Corrino.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Prelude to Dune prequel trilogy (1999–2001) by Brian Herbert and Anderson: Dune: House Atreides (1999), Dune: House Harkonnen (2000), and Dune: House Corrino (2001)"
verifications.reasoning: Exact titles and trilogy confirmed.

verifications.claim: Caladan Trilogy consists of The Duke of Caladan, The Lady of Caladan, The Heir of Caladan.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Caladan Trilogy (2020–2022) by Brian Herbert and Anderson: Dune: The Duke of Caladan (2020), Dune: The Lady of Caladan (2021), Dune: The Heir of Caladan (2022)"
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to trilogy composition.
